PullRequest.Title: Automations: Ignore irrelevant unavailable providers
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add provider-neutral evidence for whether a Sessions provider is known to own Automations
- ignore unavailable providers with no ownership evidence when computing aggregate catalogue completeness
- retain truthful unavailable state for provider-scoped legacy rows and previously authoritative non-empty Agent Host catalogues
- preserve migration, routing, tools, and accessible UI behavior by correcting the shared service state rather than suppressing the warning

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint for all changed TypeScript files
- 35 focused ProviderAutomationService and AgentHostAutomationStore tests

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restore and initial provider registration/catalogue aggregation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The BlockRestore Automations contribution instantiates IAutomationService and continuously reads aggregate automations; catalogue state is also observed by the Automations UI/new-badge flows. The new provider ownership check is a synchronous observable boolean read and adds no awaited work to restore.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the legacy Automation ledger from application storage during AutomationStore construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One legacy ledger read when the delayed aggregate service is instantiated, independent of provider or automation count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same legacy ledger was read before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous service initialization work; the added hasKnownAutomations derived reads the already-loaded in-memory array only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to the Agent Host Automation catalogue when a supported provider connection creates AgentHostAutomationStore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subscription per connected Agent Host provider/store lifecycle, not per automation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalogue subscription was established before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing provider initialization work; the PR does not create another subscription or wait for another response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered providers for aggregate state mapping; normally a small provider set. The new ownership read is O(1) for AutomationStore and reads a cached derived boolean for Agent Host stores.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalogue aggregation and autoruns execute synchronously; existing provider registration and migration sequencing are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Observable derived values cache their current result. Legacy rows are already loaded into memory; Agent Host automations are already continuously observed by the BlockRestore contribution, so ownership checks reuse the existing projection rather than introduce another projection pass.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor and observer call paths, existing BlockRestore observer, and all added reads were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact provider counts and catalogue sizes vary, but no new expensive boundary or independently repeated collection projection is introduced on this path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added work is bounded in-memory observable bookkeeping and does not move boundary work onto startup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connected Agent Host catalogue updates, including create/delete and run-summary changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An Agent Host catalogue event updates the existing subscription, invalidates catalogue projections, and notifies existing UI/context observers. The new reconnect autorun records whether the latest ready catalogue has any projected Automations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive and reduce Agent Host Automation catalogue action envelopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One received envelope per host catalogue mutation; host-side actions can update definitions and run summaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalogue envelopes were received and reduced before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing source of catalogue updates. The diff adds no dispatch, subscription, or response round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Project catalogue entries into editor-facing Automation descriptors and sort them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached derived recomputation over the effective catalogue per invalidating catalogue update while observed; O(number of catalogue entries).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The BlockRestore context-key autorun already kept aggregate and provider automations projections live on every catalogue update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This projection was already continuously observed by AutomationsCustomViewContribution at BlockRestore. hasKnownAutomations reads that cached observable and checks length, so the PR does not add a second projection in the product path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Authoritative Agent Host catalogue entry count and catalogue update frequency. The added final operation is a constant-time length comparison/set after the existing cached projection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalogue event handling and observable recomputation are synchronous and serialized by the event stream; the PR adds no task fan-out or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentHostAutomationStore.automations is a derived observable shared by the aggregate UI observer and the new hasKnownAutomations derived. Reconnectable state stores one boolean and updates it only while the authoritative catalogue is ready.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new autorun dependency and existing always-on BlockRestore automations observer were both traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large catalogues could make the pre-existing projection expensive, but product wiring already paid that cost and the diff does not materially increase its multiplicity.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new boolean snapshot does not duplicate the existing collection projection or add boundary traffic.

Scenarios.Scenario: Provider disconnect, unsupported/disabled transition, and reconnect
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Connection lifecycle transitions update authority state; aggregate catalogue state now consults retained ownership evidence only when a provider is unavailable. Reconnect initialization and migration behavior remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish or release the existing Agent Host connection/catalogue subscription during reconnect lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active AgentHostAutomationStore/subscription for the provider; replacement is serialized by synchronous connection binding updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: setConnection already created the same store and initiated the same migration before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing reconnect work. The new retained boolean neither starts a connection nor delays readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read provider-scoped legacy Automation rows from the already-instantiated legacy store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One in-memory observable read per ownership recomputation; underlying storage is not reread by the added code.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy store construction and storage refresh behavior were unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No filesystem boundary on the changed path; storage change handling remains event-driven and pre-existing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Reconnect frequency, provider count, and whether legacy/current catalogues contain any rows. Retained state is one boolean per reconnectable provider and remains bounded for the store lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connection binding owns one current store and clears the prior binding before replacement. Existing migration uses its retry/sequencing behavior; no new asynchronous work or concurrency burst is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The last authoritative ownership state is explicitly coalesced into one observable boolean; it is overwritten on each ready catalogue and released with the registered store. Cold reconnect still uses existing subscription initialization; warm in-process disconnect reads the retained boolean.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership, disposal registration, and reconnect state transitions were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reconnect frequency varies, but each transition adds only bounded synchronous state updates.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. State retention is bounded and lifecycle-owned, with no new boundary calls or critical-path waits.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and relevant call paths. The PR adds provider ownership evidence through derived observables and a disposed autorun, but introduces no new expensive boundary, unbounded retention, concurrency fan-out, or material duplicate projection. No findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
